title: Our likes and feelings
kc: Children should be able to demonstrate self knowledge about likes, dislikes, fear, thoughts, and what they enjoy.
cols: Information about particular things a child likes or dislikes. -Similarities and differences - Based on the current theme, every child is given opportunity to say what he/she likes, dislikes, fears, how he/she feels during a certain activity. For example: colors, clothes, types of food, drinks, animals, plants, games, and so on; and he/she can draw where possible. - In a guided discussion, children recognize things they have in common and differences and also things they like that can harm their life based on what each one said. - Children form small groups based on what they like or other similarities. For example; those who like most mangoes, bananas. They identify a group with more members. - In small groups, children discuss the story read to them showing feelings, characters’ thoughts then compare with theirs. - They play games: What do you like? -Demonstrate what they like, enjoy, dislike, fear, and their thoughts. - Discover similarities with others - Recognize differences between him/her and peers as well as adults. - Build self- confidence - Feel free to tell their likes, thoughts, and dislikes - Respect everybody for their differences.
assess: ability to demonstrate self knowledge by telling what they like, fear, dislike, and give their opinions.
res: pieces of paper, pens, different types of fruits, materials related to the current theme.
parent: listen to children and consider what they like, enjoy, need and help them to change where necessary.

title: Controlling emotions
kc: Children should be able to appropriately show and control their emotions with self-confidence.
cols: Showing emotions. - Controlling emotions. - In small groups, children play games that help them to be organized. For example: dancing until a song is over without stopping. Playing until the game is over; - All children participate in games helping them to show their emotions: happiness, sorrow, sadness, anger, fear... - In small groups, a child imitates someone’s emotions through actions and gestures and the rest of the children recognize emotions based on how his/her face looks. - Each child draws pictures of things they want to do or own, and explains why. - All children listen to a story about someone who failed to controll his/her emotions, and could not think appropriately; someone who was selfish and forgot others or either of the two. They answer questions about the story showing the importance of controlling emotions, thinking appropriately, and caring for others instead of self. - All children strive to get used to waiting, caring for others, and controlling emotions through everyday activities at school and at home with the assistance of teachers and parents. - State the importance controlling emotions, waiting and following instructions. - Controll his/her emotions - Demonstrate patience while waiting for something. - Communicate his thoughts and needs - Feel sorry for people whose needs are not satisfied - Build self- confidence. - Show patience and persistence. - Show empathy toward those who are suffering. - Show respect toward those who are different from him/her. - Develop teamwork.
assess: ability to show and control their emotions, care for and work with others with self confidence.
res: materials for different games, and those for cleaning.
parent: show trust toward children, interact with them and listen to them, teach them to appropriately show their emotions, control them and care for others; show sympathy to a child facing difficulties by comforting him/her.

title: Engage cooperatively
kc: Children should be able to work with peers, empathize with them in different circumstances and strive to settle conflict peacefully.
cols: Protecting life - Healthy relationships and working together with others - Settling conflict peacefully - In small groups, children show circumstances where they can face challenges and how to avoid them. - In small groups, children play cooperative games and get the opportunity to discuss how to care for their colleagues who are facing challenges: sick, those who lost their relatives. - In small groups, children role play cooperation, care for others and conflict resolution. - Children answer questions from stories about rescuing others which characterise the Rwandan culture; stories about someone who is sad, fearful; they share opinions about how to help such people. - In pairs, children do different activities together: matching parts of a picture, building, cleaning the table, writing stories that will be displayed in the classroom. - In games and in everyday activities, at school and at home, children get opportunity to work with others, behave carefully torward others, care for others, and resolve conflicts with the assistance of teachers and parents. - Explain the importance of working together to resolve conflicts peacefully - Tell what they can do to avoid hurting others - Tell what they can do to help and work with others - Join others in games and other school and home related activities - Show that they care about their safety and that of others - Settle conflicts peacefully - Care for others - Help and support those in difficult circumstances - Avoid hurtful words and activities towards others - Feel apologetic towards someone they’ve hurt - Forgive others - Avoid fighting - Be honest
assess: ability to work together with their peers, care for others, empathize with them and strive for solving conflicts in a peaceful way. [[-119-218 p90]] 198
res: story books, balls and other teaching materials that can be used in different games.
parent: cooperate with children, be a good role model to them in terms of peaceful conflict resolution in their home, in having healthy relationships with others, showing empathy to people who are going through difficulties, apologizing and forgiving.

title: Caring for and respecting
kc: Children will be able to show appropriate conduct toward others, care for and respect their peers, relatives and other people in different circumstances.
cols: Respectful conduct: Greeting one another, answering, eating and drinking, dressing, talking to others - Appropriate conduct toward different people: young and adult. - In small groups, children dramatise the roles of adults and young. - Children play showing politeness, respect, helping the needy, caring for adults and their peers. - All children listen to a story about someone who behaved badly in a certain place; they give their opinions about the appropriate behaviour the person ought to show. - Each child draws people having celebrations in their families, at church or in the neighborhood. Each child is given opportunity to show what he/she drew, and all together talk about appropriate conduct that should characterize children in different places and circumstances. - In everyday life, at home and at school, children do activities helping them to develop kindness, care for others, respect for adults and young, the culture of greeting and saying goodbye to their teachers and other children as well as other things that help them improve their discipline. - Children answer questions from the story about issues that young children may face such as kidnapping, rape, and discuss appropriate behaviour in such circumstances. - Tell how they can behave in different circumstances, and in front of different people. - State the characteristics of a polite child. - Use a polite and respectful language. - Participate in family, friends and neighbours’ activities. - Carry out activities aimed to care for others. - Recognize people with ill/evil plans. - Care for others, - Respect teachers. - Say “No” in order to protect themselves. - Request for help when necessary. - Respect their peers. - Avoid insulting people.
res: materials that can be used in role plays and games.
parent: teach children to be polite and respect all people by setting a good example; help them to know their rights and responsibilities.

title: I am curious!
kc: Children should be able to choose and engage in familiar activities that they want to do in their everyday life, and the new experiences so as to satisfy their curiosity.
cols: Being curious and motivated to discover and use materials found at school in different activities. - In small groups, children play a game of guessing objects that are hidden in a bag by just touching, without opening. They can even smell different things that are kept inside a bottle, and guess what they are. - In small groups, children are given opportunity to observe, touch, smell different objects and ask questions to satisfy their curiosity. The teacher avoids things that can harm children. - In small groups, children observe pictures on the cover page of a given book and ask questions with aim to know the story inside. They find answers together. - In pairs, children play a game called “I am a spy”, whereby one takes the lead. “I spy using my eye”, or any other object found around - In small groups or individually, children get opportunity to choose an activity to carry out, the needed materials and techniques they will use in all topic areas where applicable. - Explain how they feel, and how they behave when they are curious. - Choose an activity, materials and techniques to do the activity. - Ask questions of curiosity about certain topic areas or materials. - Show motivation to use a given material. - Participate voluntarily in scheduled activities. - Build self- confidence.
assess: ability to demonstrate their curiosity about familiar and and new experiences.
res: the bag with different objects and other materials related to chosen activities, bottles or other objects to recognize through smelling.
parent: answer questions frequently asked by children, surprise children with things they like (giving them gifts, reminding them of their birthdays)

title: We can work hard
kc: Children should be able to demonstrate perseverance in a range of challenging learning activities and resistence to distractions.
cols: Concentrate on an activity - In pairs,children choose an activity, and strive to achieve their goal; - All children, at home or at school, participate in listening games. For example: Simon says “lift up your hands”, and they execute ; - Children engage in activities for extended period of time, requiring perseverance. These activities are neither too easy nor too challenging for children to loose interest and give up. - Show the importance of developing concentration and persistence in learning though it may be difficult. - Concentrate on an activity with dedication. - Demonstrate perseverance in an activity though it is more challenging and frustrating. - Enjoy working hard. - Strive for perfection. - Enjoy the result after difficulties. - Strive to overcome challenges.
assess: ability to concentrate on an activity, persistence in case of difficulties/challenges and removing distractions.
parent: encourage their children to persevere and concentrate on what they started before starting a new activity; set a goal and strive to achive it.
